reviews.title: Not great
reviews.text:
I think the idea to use clips from real Japanese shows and animes is a pretty good one, and I think it’s useful to hear real world examples of words being spoken in different contexts by different people to be able to pick up those same words in daily conversation.

However in Umi’s case it’s just very poorly executed. Aside from the fact that the UI is partially AI generated and some of the clips don’t load always, there just isn’t much elaboration on the new words that are introduced to you in these video clip “lessons”. It just goes from here’s a new word, to here’s a new word, to here’s a new word, without any kind of practice interphase on how to use it, why you’d use it, etc.. it’s just kind of lazy and definitely not going to help you go deep into language learning. 

Sure, it could help you with learning some new words to implement in your language speaking skills that you have to inevitably pick up from another program but as a standalone product I can’t think of anyone making meaningful progress with just this as a tool, which may not be the purpose of it anyways. 

I think if you’re starting from scratch this app is definitely not for you, but the only reason I made this review is because I think the app is genuinely a great idea and could be a great product if executed properly, it’s just a shame it’s kind of one dimensional and shallow and I hope the devs could put more effort into it, then they could really have a unique and engaging product on their hands.

reviews.title: Good start but needs work
reviews.text:
First off, I'm using it to learn Japanese and have been using it daily for more than a week now.

The good:
- Hearing and seeing words used in context and made into simple video "flash cards" is cool. It works relatively well. 

- The review feature hiding the different sections until you click is appreciated.

- Drawing practice is a nice tool, but I wish it included proper stroke order. Also, not a huge deal, but you do have to manually choose "pass" or "fail" rather than the app detecting it for you.

The bad:
- Semi-frequent bug where the audio cuts off and you have to close the lesson and reopen it to fix.

- I've seen various issues with translation of words being confusing/not quite accurate. You can report issues like this in the app, but there's no insight to if that actually does anything or if anyone has read the reports. After about a week of using the app I've found ~4 minor translation issues that I've reported through the app.

- Some of the videos are literally just the vocab word said once and that's it which feels completely useless for this type of learning.

- On "review" it asks "again, hard, good, easy" but it's not clear what that means or does. Also, it gives you no option to enter an answer, so it's more like a flashcard than a review quiz.

- What's the point of the "watch" section? It doesn't show new content with vocab you've learned (which is what I was hoping it would be for). The review section already exists, so why would I use the "watch" section..?

- The app seems to be using some kind of spaced repetition, but seems almost nonsensical in the way it determines the next review timing. To the dev: you should follow WaniKani's example more closely.

- There's no clear rhyme or reason behind the ordering of vocab lessons. Seems like words were chosen randomly? If they weren't, there was never an explanation given as to why the order is the way it is.

Overall:
I enjoy the app for what it is, but it could absolutely be much better.

reviews.title: Great app - pedagogy…?
reviews.text:
Updating my last review from 3 stars to 4.

The word selection & ordering is questionable. The word “to investigate” is taught before “big”. I believe the point of the app is to help you learn in context, but wouldn’t it make sense to learn words I’d hear/use most often first?

Also the practice sections get repetitive after a while (over a year in). The courses move fast, it doesn’t seem realistic to learn four new words everyday until you’re fluent while practicing older words. Has anyone actually completed the Japanese course without prior Japanese knowledge?

reviews.title: Good for Japanese, Ok for Korean
reviews.text: I think the app worked well for learning Japanese. It has been frustrating for learning Korean though. You start a lesson by learning a word and then there are examples of the word during the lesson but they are often conjugated or modified versions of the word, none of which were explained. So not only are you trying to memorize the word, you have to deal with surprise conjugations that were never explained. Either use the exact word in the examples or explain the conjugations before showing them. This happens constantly when trying to learn Korean on the app and I have ended my subscription to go to an app which actually explains such concepts. This was not really an issue I encountered when learning Japanese through the app though.

reviews.title: Serious Issues
reviews.text:
This app feels extremely poorly made. I cannot for the life of me get the “record your voice” part of any lesson to work. I have been speaking Japanese for 5 years and am no stranger to proper pronunciation and the speed of speech, but whether I speak quickly, slowly, spell it out one by one or OVERLY-pronounce each word, nothing works. I get 0% every time because it does not pick up what I’m actually saying.
Also, translations aren’t completely accurate much of the time, and the automated voice itself even mispronounces things. this is not the biggest example, but one that I see constantly which is very annoying—は(wa) is not pronounced “ha”, it is pronounced wa within sentences. Extremely basic knowledge.
Overall, although the concept is helpful (using real speech from movies and shows), the app itself cannot keep up with the things that it is using, because there’s nothing natural about it.

reviews.title: Do Not Download. Too many bugs. Once they take your $$ they ignore you.
reviews.text:
This app sucks. It gives wrong audio languages, queues words that aren’t in the audio clip, and in general is poorly executed. The only redeeming factor is the idea of hearing the same word in different scenarios, but what’s missing is spaced repetition. I’ve asked for my money back because of how buggy the app is, but haven’t heard anything. I am rampantly recommending fellow language learners against this app.

Even the review feature in the app won’t close the keyboard when you’re done typing, so there’s no way to actually send the developer feedback other than to report a bug. And given their continued silence on that front, I doubt they’ll do anything for you once you’ve paid their fee.

Don’t download. Better off with Pimsleur and Duolingo.
